title: Tangent space and square-zero parameter algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local maps inducing the identity on $k$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a predeformation category on $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ satisfying (RS), as defined in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Then $T\mathcal F$ is naturally a $k$-vector space and, for every finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, there is a natural bijection $\overline{\mathcal F}(k[V])\cong T\mathcal F\otimes_k V$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a linear map $\lambda:V\to W$, transport along $(a,v)\mapsto(a,\lambda(v))$ corresponds to $1\otimes\lambda$. In particular if $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d$ is a basis of $T\mathcal F$ and $V$ has basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$, the class $\sum_i\theta_i\otimes v_i$ maps onto all of $T\mathcal F$ under the maps $k[V]\to k[\epsilon]$ induced by all linear functionals $V\to k$. This includes $d=0$.

proof.text: Put $F(A)=\overline{\mathcal F}(A)$ and $L(V)=F(k[V])$, with $L(f)$ induced by $(a,v)\mapsto(a,f(v))$. These ring maps preserve multiplication and compose as the linear maps do, so transport on isomorphism classes makes $L$ a covariant functor. The rings $k[V]$ belong to the test category: $(a,v)$ is a unit exactly when $a\ne0$, with inverse $(a^{-1},-a^{-2}v)$, so the maximal ideal is $V$ and the residue field is $k$; every ideal is a $k$-subspace of the finite-dimensional space $k\oplus V$, so descending chains stabilize. The isomorphism $k[U\oplus V]\to k[U]\times_k k[V]$ is $(a,u,v)\mapsto((a,u),(a,v))$. The augmentation $k[V]\to k$ is surjective, so (RS) identifies its deformation groupoid with the 2-fibre product over $\mathcal F(k)$. This last groupoid has isomorphism classes exactly $F(k[U])\times F(k[V])$: between any two objects of $\mathcal F(k)$ there is exactly one arrow, since that groupoid is equivalent to the terminal groupoid. Thus a pair of objects admits exactly one gluing arrow, and every pair of component isomorphisms respects that arrow. Taking isomorphism classes gives the bijection $c_{U,V}:L(U\oplus V)\to L(U)\times L(V)$. Also $L(0)=F(k)$ is a singleton.

source.place: Tag 06IH (lemma-tangent-space-vector-space), product-preservation input; here obtained directly from the definition of (RS), rather than through Tags 06J7 and 06I0.

proof.text: Apply the product-preserving functor linearization lemma to the functor $L$ of step 1. Its hypotheses hold for every finite-dimensional pair, including zero. It supplies canonical vector structures on all $L(V)$, linear maps $L(f)$ and linearity in $f$. In particular $L(k)=F(k[\epsilon])=T\mathcal F$ is a $k$-vector space. Addition is $L(+):L(k\oplus k)\to L(k)$ after the inverse product comparison, and multiplication by $a$ is induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$, exactly the deformation operations.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), as used by Tags 06IA (lemma-tangent-space-functor) and 06IH (lemma-tangent-space-vector-space).

proof.text: Write $T=L(k)$. For $v\in V$, let $f_v:k\to V$ send $1$ to $v$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto L(f_v)(x)$ is bilinear: it is linear in $x$ because $L(f_v)$ is linear, and linear in $v$ because $f_{av+bw}=af_v+bf_w$ and $L$ is linear on maps. The tensor universal property gives $\Phi_V:T\otimes_k V\to L(V)$ with $\Phi_V(x\otimes v)=L(f_v)(x)$. Choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $V$, with coordinates $p_i:V\to k$. The inverse is explicitly $\Psi_V(z)=\sum_i L(p_i)(z)\otimes e_i$. Indeed, on a pure tensor, $\Psi_V\Phi_V(x\otimes v)=\sum_i p_i(v)x\otimes e_i=x\otimes v$ by bilinearity and $v=\sum_i p_i(v)e_i$; pure tensors generate. Conversely $\Phi_V\Psi_V(z)=\sum_i L(f_{e_i}p_i)(z)=L(\sum_i f_{e_i}p_i)(z)=z$. For $r=0$, $L(V)=L(0)$ is the zero vector space, and the tensor product is zero because every pure tensor has second factor zero. This proves bijectivity in every finite dimension. The construction of $\Phi_V$ uses no basis, so the resulting bijection and its inverse are canonical.

source.place: Tag 06I8 (lemma-linear-functor-over-field), explicit pure-tensor construction and finite-basis inverse; used by Tag 06IH.

proof.text: For $\lambda:V\to W$ and a pure tensor, $L(\lambda)\Phi_V(x\otimes v)=L(\lambda f_v)(x)=L(f_{\lambda(v)})(x)=\Phi_W(x\otimes\lambda(v))$. Both sides are linear maps and pure tensors generate, so $L(\lambda)\Phi_V=\Phi_W(1\otimes\lambda)$. By step 1, $L(\lambda)$ is exactly transport along $(a,v)\mapsto(a,\lambda(v))$. For $W=k$, identify $T\otimes_k k$ with $T$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ (inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$); the same formula for $\Phi_k$ gives this identification.

source.place: Tag 06I8 (lemma-linear-functor-over-field), formula for the natural isomorphism; Tag 06IH, functoriality in V.

proof.text: For the final clause assume the stated finite bases $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d$ of $T$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$. Step 4 sends $\sum_i\theta_i\otimes v_i$ under a functional $\ell:V\to k$ to $\sum_i\ell(v_i)\theta_i$. Every $t\in T$ has a basis expansion $t=\sum_i a_i\theta_i$. The functional $\ell(\sum_i b_i v_i)=\sum_i b_i a_i$ has $\ell(v_i)=a_i$, hence gives precisely $t$. If $d=0$, both spaces are zero; the empty tensor sum and the unique functional give the unique element of $T$, so surjectivity still holds.

source.place: Tag 06IH (lemma-tangent-space-vector-space), functorial tensor identification; elementary finite-basis evaluation consequence needed for the versal-object construction.
